title: Diraq Installs Silicon Spin Quantum Computer in Equinix Commercial Data Center - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Diraq installed an operational 8-qubit silicon-spin quantum computer in an Equinix commercial data center in Sydney (<20 kW, 172 sq ft) and plans a 256-qubit chip swap within the same footprint, testing whether CMOS-fabricated spin qubits can scale inside ordinary colocation facilities.

insights.claim: Diraq deployed an operational eight-qubit electron-spin-in-silicon quantum computer inside an Equinix commercial data center in Sydney, Australia, drawing under 20 kW and occupying 172 square feet.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Data-center-compatible quantum hardware could open colocation operators like Equinix as quantum distribution channels.

insights.claim: Operating a quantum processor in an active data center exposes the dilution refrigerator and control electronics to electromagnetic interference, cooling-water flow fluctuations and floor vibrations absent from academic labs; the Equinix deployment will baseline uptime, gate-fidelity stability and control drift.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch the published uptime/fidelity metrics — they will validate or undercut the data-center quantum thesis.
insights.locator: Operating a quantum processor within an active data center

insights.claim: Diraq plans within twelve months to install a 256-qubit processor in the existing refrigeration unit, testing whether qubit capacity can scale via modular chip swaps without expanding facility infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If chip swaps scale capacity 32x in place, the capex profile of silicon spin compares favorably to modalities needing bespoke plants.
insights.locator: The system operates using quantum dots

insights.claim: Diraq projects utility-scale systems of more than 2 million qubits on a single die by 2031, at roughly 300 kW peak draw and about 54 sq ft (5 m²) footprint, using industrial CMOS wafer manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Long-dated roadmap claim; the investment case for silicon spin rests on leveraging standard semiconductor fabs.

insights.claim: Diraq's qubits are quantum dots fabricated with standard silicon-metal-oxide-semiconductor (Si-MOS) lithography, which it positions as integrable into enterprise facilities unlike modalities requiring bespoke physical plants.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CMOS compatibility ties silicon-spin progress to existing foundry capacity.
insights.locator: The system operates using quantum dots

insights.claim: Diraq's Quantum at Work white paper models that a 10-percentage-point improvement in drug candidate success rates from quantum simulation could cut drug development costs by roughly $600 million per approved molecule.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Company-internal model; useful as a pharma TAM framing but not independent evidence.

insights.claim: Diraq was selected for Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative and holds a $38 million non-binding preliminary memorandum of terms under the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government validation and potential CHIPS funding de-risk Diraq's path; non-binding status is a caveat.
insights.locator: The deployment builds on Diraq’s selection
